question: After a fixed `imsg` release exists, should OpenClaw make that release a hard startup floor and retire the persisted coalescing option and client-side fallback?
rationale: The final transition intentionally turns previously accepted configuration and binaries into doctor- and upgrade-required states, so maintainers must approve the compatibility policy even after the delivery defect is fixed.

options.title: Require fixed release and proof
options.body: Raise the floor to the first released `imsg` containing the GUID-linked preview fix and merge only after exact-head upgrade and one-turn delivery proof.

options.title: Retain OpenClaw fallback
options.body: Keep the existing option and compatibility path until maintainers are ready to require the config and binary upgrade together.

recommendation.title: Require fixed release and proof
recommendation.body: Raise the floor to the first released `imsg` containing the GUID-linked preview fix and merge only after exact-head upgrade and one-turn delivery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily concerns the supported `imsg` release floor and OpenClaw operator-upgrade policy.
